title: the coronation planned
hook: the king says tomorrow, and tells his son a hard truth about hearts

segments.voice: Yesterday: the coronation planned, part one. An old king asked his assembly, and the hall roared yes. Did you keep count of one kindness? Today, the date is set, and it's sooner than anyone expected. Day five hundred fifteen.

Some decisions are made slowly and carried out slowly. Some are made slowly and then, all at once, rushed. You've probably seen it: the plan everyone agreed on for months, suddenly happening this weekend, because someone got nervous. That's where Dasharatha is today. The assembly has said yes. The obvious next step is to set a good day, send the invitations, call Bharata home. Instead, the king sends for Rama twice in one day, and the second time, his voice is urgent.
screen: `SLOW DECISION, SUDDEN RUSH.` → `SENT FOR TWICE IN ONE DAY.`

segments.voice: First Rama comes to his father's hall, bows, and hears the news in public. The king tells him to keep up his good habits and rule gently. Rama goes home. Then the charioteer Sumantra comes back for him. The king wants you again. This time Dasharatha speaks privately, and he sounds afraid. I've had bad dreams, he says. Meteors have fallen with a crash. The astrologers say my star is under pressure from harsh planets. When signs like this come, a king can lose his life, or fall into trouble. So the coronation will be tomorrow. Then he says something very honest, and a little chilling. Do it now, while Bharata is away from the city. Bharata is good, he says, devoted to his elder brother, self-controlled, kind. But the minds of people change, even the minds of good people. The king isn't accusing anyone. He's admitting he doesn't trust time. Rama listens and goes to tell his mother, Kausalya, who has been praying for exactly this. Then the priest Vasishtha visits Rama's house with instructions. Tonight, you and Sita keep a fast. Sleep on the ground, on a bed of sacred grass. Rama and Sita bathe, make an offering, and spend the night quietly in a shrine, ready for morning. Notice the shape of today. The love is real. The plan is good. And the hurry is where the danger lives. A king who once asked an entire assembly for its opinion now wants it finished before his own son can come home.
screen: `RAMA HEARS IT IN PUBLIC.` · `BAD DREAMS AND FALLING STARS.` · `DO IT WHILE BHARATA IS AWAY.` · `A FAST ON SACRED GRASS.` · then, large: `THE HURRY IS WHERE THE DANGER LIVES.`

segments.voice: Sit, and notice if anything in you is rushing right now: a deadline, a reply you want to send, a decision you want over with. Name it to yourself in a few words. Then slow the breath on purpose: a little longer in, a little longer out. You don't have to drop the plan. Just let it wait the length of this sit, and see what it looks like afterward. The bell holds the time.
The coronation planned, and rushed. Shaken by omens, Dasharatha sets it for tomorrow, while Bharata is away, and Rama and Sita keep a fast through the night.
Your line: the coronation planned. Today, before you rush something good, ask who it leaves out. Day five hundred fifteen.

howItsDone: Fasting and keeping vigil the night before a major rite is a common Hindu practice; in the text, Vasishtha instructs Rama and Sita to fast and sleep on kusha grass before the consecration.

match.prompt: the night before — tap the pairs.
pairs: part of the king's bad omens
tells Rama and Sita to fast

myth: he calls Bharata good; he only says people's minds can change.
the king moves the coronation to the next day
he's shaken by bad dreams and omens.
Rama and Sita spend the night feasting
they fast and sleep on sacred grass, as Vasishtha instructs.

fork.setup: you're Dasharatha. the omens frighten you and the assembly has agreed. when do you crown Rama?
options: in a month, with every king invited.
fork.reveal: he says tomorrow, and tells Rama plainly: while Bharata is away, because even good minds can change.

original.note: Sanskrit upavāsa: a fast, literally staying near. Rama and Sita keep one the night before the rite.

trapdoor: what you thought: the coronation was planned slowly and carefully.
what it means: after a careful assembly, the king rushes it to the next day, afraid of omens.
what a scholar hears: readers have long argued about why the king wanted it done while Bharata was away; the text gives his fear of omens and of changing minds, and leaves the rest to us.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 3–4 (Rama summoned twice; omens; 'while Bharata is away')
Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 5–6 (Vasishtha's instructions; the fast and vigil)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
The omens (dreams, meteors, the king's birth-star afflicted by the sun, Mars and Rahu) are summarized; confirm.
Dasharatha's line that even good people's minds can change (Ayodhya 4): paraphrased; confirm.
upavāsa 'staying near' is the standard literal sense (upa + vas); confirm the note is acceptable.
